newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia, Abkhaz separatists pledge peace.
newsitem.headline: Georgia, Abkhaz separatists pledge peace.

text.p: Face-to-face talks between Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze and Abkhaz separatist leader Vladislav Ardzinba ended on Friday with the signing of a joint statement to resolve their differences peacefully.
But they reported no breakthrough on an overall political agreement that would put an end to the conflict, which claimed 10,000 lives in 1992-93 ethnic fighting.

The joint statement signed by Shevardnadze and Ardzinba said the sides agreed "to take upon themselves the obligation not to use arms to resolve differences between them and under no circumstances to allow a resumption of bloodshed".

"Only peaceful political methods through negotiations should be used," it went on. It said the two sides "managed to agree on a series of key problems on resolving the conflict. But at the same time, there remain significant differences".

Ardzinba's surprise visit was his first to Tbilisi since the war began exactly five years ago, when Georgian government troops marched into the subtropical province on the Black Sea to put down moves towards independence.
Abkhazia has had de facto independence since routing the Georgian government forces but has not been recognised by any state.
